sources.title: CUAD buyer-side triage rubric
sources.scope: Defines the project's severity thresholds, missing-clause treatment, and deterministic contract rollup for the ten selected categories.
sources.limitations: A reproducible project convention, not law, market-standard evidence, or legal advice.

sources.title: CUAD category descriptions
sources.scope: Defines what text belongs to each CUAD clause category.
sources.limitations: CUAD category membership and expert span annotations are not risk ratings.

sources.title: CUAD: An Expert-Annotated NLP Dataset for Legal Contract Review
sources.scope: Documents the 510-contract, 41-category CUAD corpus and the boundary between extraction and contextual legal counseling.
sources.limitations: Does not provide buyer-side Low/Medium/High risk ground truth.

sources.title: Contracting Principles
sources.scope: Provides balanced contracting considerations for assignment, audit, IP, liability, insurance, termination, warranties, and related terms.
sources.limitations: Principles require transaction-specific selection and applicable-law review; they are not universal legal rules.

sources.title: Risk Allocation and Pricing Approaches guidance note
sources.issuing_body: UK Cabinet Office and Government Legal Department
sources.scope: Supports transparent, proportional, context-sensitive allocation of contractual risk.
sources.limitations: Useful methodology and drafting benchmark only; it is not controlling authority for U.S. commercial contracts.

sources.title: Contract Risk Assessment
sources.scope: Demonstrates discrete Low/Medium/High procurement triage factors and escalation based on individual High factors.
sources.limitations: Institution-specific precedent for scale design, not substantive ground truth for CUAD contracts.

sources.title: Exclusive Dealing or Requirements Contracts
sources.scope: Explains that exclusivity is common and generally lawful but can require contextual competition review.
sources.limitations: Does not make every exclusive clause high risk or determine enforceability in an individual transaction.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0
sources.issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.scope: Supports documenting provenance, assumptions, limitations, uncertainty, and evaluation boundaries.
sources.limitations: Governs dataset and model documentation; it does not define substantive contract risk.
